transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I came in because... I just barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself anymore. Like, trying new recipes. I used to love cooking and I'd go to the farmer's market to get all these fresh ingredients. Actually, the last time I went, there was this guy selling these huge purple heirloom tomatoes, and he was telling me this whole long story about how his grandfather brought the seeds over from Italy. I tried growing tomatoes once on my apartment balcony, but the squirrels kept eating them before they even got ripe. They are so bold around here, they'd just sit on the railing and stare at me while taking bites out of them. I even bought this special netting, but they chewed right through it. 

But, um... yeah, anyway. The cooking, or my dance class, hiking, even game night with my friends... I don't know, they all just sit there now. It's like they're just chores that I keep putting off.
Do you still enjoy things when you're actually doing them, even if you don't feel like starting them?

Not really... like I was just saying, it all just feels like a chore now, even when I force myself to do it. I just don't care about them anymore. Like, I went to game night a couple weeks ago because my friend Sarah practically dragged me out of my house. She's always been pushy like that, ever since we were in high school. We actually met in detention, which is funny because she's like, this super strict accountant now and does everybody's taxes. 

Anyway, she made me play this new board game with all these little wooden pieces... meeples, I think they call them? I kept dropping mine under the table, and her dog—this little pug mix that snorts constantly—kept trying to eat them. We had to spend like twenty minutes crawling around on the rug looking for a yellow wooden farmer. It was a whole mess, and he had dog drool all over him when we found him. 

But um... yeah. Even sitting there playing it, I just didn't care. I didn't feel like myself at all. I just kept looking at the clock wanting to go home.
Do you still feel pleasure when you're doing things that you used to enjoy?

I mean... I think I kind of just said that, right? Like, no, I don't really feel any pleasure from them. It's all just flat. 

Like when I tried going back to my dance class a while ago. It’s at this local community center, and the instructor, Brenda, she always wears these wild neon leggings. The last time I went, she had on this pair with actual glitter glued to them, and it was shedding everywhere on the hardwood floor while we were moving around. The janitor—Gary, I think his name is, he’s this older guy who always wears his baseball cap backwards—he was looking through the little window in the door and he looked so mad about the glitter everywhere. Gary is usually super nice, though. He actually helped me jumpstart my car once when I accidentally left the interior lights on overnight. My car battery is so old, I really need to take it to the shop, but the mechanics always try to upsell you on air filters and wiper blades and stuff, you know? It's like, I just want a basic oil change, I don't need you to rebuild my whole engine or charge me fifty dollars for a piece of paper. 

But, um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, no. Even when I'm right in the middle of doing something I used to love, I just don't feel anything good from it.
Have you experienced a loss of interest in activities and a loss of pleasure at the same time, or has one happened before the other?

I think they kind of happened at the same time? Like, I just stopped caring about all of it. I mean, that's why I came in, because I just barely care about anything that used to make me feel like myself. The dance class, hiking, trying new recipes... even game night, like I said. They all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. 

Speaking of chores, I really need to clean out my fridge. I bought all this produce from the farmer's market, like those purple tomatoes, and I know they're just rotting in the crisper drawer right now. It's so gross when vegetables get all slimy, you know? And then you have to scrub the whole drawer out, and it never really smells the same again. My mom used to put a box of baking soda in the fridge to stop smells, but I never remember to buy baking soda. I don't even bake. I tried making banana bread once during lockdown like everyone else, but I forgot to add the baking powder or whatever makes it rise, and it came out like a dense, wet brick. I ended up throwing it out for the birds, but even the crows wouldn't touch it. Crows are so smart, though. I watched this documentary where they showed crows solving puzzles to get food. They're basically little geniuses. 

But, um... yeah. The interest and the pleasure, it just all went away together. It's all just a chore now.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, it's been a while now. This has been going on since the robbery at that festival job I had... so about two years and three months ago. 

That festival was supposed to be so much fun, too. It was this big outdoor music and arts thing, and they had all these food trucks lined up. I remember there was this one truck that only sold gourmet grilled cheese sandwiches. They had one with brie and fig jam on sourdough, and the line for it was always like a mile long. The guy running it had this massive beard, like a lumberjack, but he was wearing a bright pink apron. I always wondered how hot it got inside those trucks during the summer. It has to be like an oven in there, right? Especially standing over a grill all day. My cousin worked in a kitchen once, and she said she used to put ice cubes in her bra just to survive the dinner rush. She eventually quit and went to cosmetology school. She cuts my hair now, actually, though she always cuts the bangs a little too short. I tell her just a trim, and then I walk out looking like I’m in a 90s punk band. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, it's been about two years and three months since the festival thing happened. That's when all this started.
Have you been having any thoughts that you're worthless or that you'd be better off dead?

No, I don't really think like that. I don't feel worthless or anything, and I definitely don't want to be dead. 

I actually watched this whole series on near-death experiences the other night because I couldn't sleep. It was on one of those streaming services my ex-roommate still pays for—she moved out like three years ago, but I guess she forgot to change her password on my TV. She was always forgetting things like that. One time she left the front door wide open when she went to work. Just... wide open. Anybody could have walked right in. My neighbor's cat actually did walk in. He's this huge orange tabby named Marmalade, and he just made himself right at home on our couch. We tried to get him off, but he hissed at us, so we just let him sleep there all afternoon. Cats are so bossy, you know? They just own whatever space they're in. I kind of wish I had that kind of confidence sometimes. Just walk into a room and act like I own the place. 

But, no, to answer your question... I don't have thoughts about being dead or feeling worthless. Just... everything feels like a chore, like I said.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't think I'm moving slow or talking slow. 

My aunt talks really slow, though. Like, agonizingly slow. She draws out every single vowel when she tells a story, and she always tells these really long stories about her garden. She grows these massive prize-winning zucchinis, and she's always trying to give them away because you can only eat so much zucchini bread, right? She brought one over last summer that was the size of a baseball bat. I actually used it as a doorstop for a few days before it started getting soft. I probably should have composted it, but I don't really understand composting. Like, you just put garbage in a bin and wait for it to turn into dirt? It seems like it would just attract raccoons. We have these raccoons in my neighborhood that are so bold, they'll literally stare you down if you catch them in the trash. One of them actually stole a bag of hot dog buns right off my patio table when I turned my back for two seconds. 

But um, yeah, I don't think I'm moving or talking any slower than normal.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

No, my weight's been pretty steady, actually. I haven't noticed my clothes fitting any differently or anything. 

Speaking of clothes, though, I was trying to organize my closet the other day, and I found this old denim jacket I used to wear all the time in high school. It has all these pins on the collar—like band logos and those little sarcastic sayings people used to put on everything. I had one that said "I'm not arguing, I'm just explaining why I'm right." I thought I was so edgy back then. I actually wore that jacket to my first concert. It was an outdoor venue, and it rained the entire time. We were all completely soaked, and my friend lost one of her shoes in the mud. Just one shoe. She had to walk all the way back to the car with one bare foot, stepping on gravel and everything. We stopped at a 24-hour diner afterward, and she wrapped her foot in a bunch of napkins so the waitress wouldn't notice. We ordered a huge plate of chili cheese fries, and they gave us so much cheese it was basically soup. I haven't had chili cheese fries in forever. There's this place downtown that supposedly makes the best ones, but parking down there is such a nightmare, it's not even worth it. You have to parallel park on this massive hill, and I'm always terrified my brakes are just going to give out and I'll roll backwards into someone's Mercedes. 

But, uh, no. No weight loss or anything like that.
Have you been feeling restless or having trouble sitting still lately?

No, I don't think so. I haven't felt restless or anything like that. I can sit still just fine. 

Actually, sitting still is basically all I do when I go to my sister's house. She has this giant sectional couch that is so deep, once you sit down, you're practically trapped in it. It's like quicksand, but made of velvet. She got it on sale because it's this really obnoxious mustard yellow color, but she says it adds a "pop" to the living room. I think it just looks like a giant hot dog bun, honestly. She's always trying to get me to help her redecorate, but her taste is so chaotic. She bought these curtains last month that have giant peacocks printed all over them. And not just the feathers—like, the whole bird. Who wants giant birds staring at them while they're trying to watch TV? We were watching this documentary about deep-sea diving, and I swear the peacock on the curtain was judging me the whole time. Deep-sea diving is terrifying, by the way. Just the idea of being down in the pitch black with all that pressure... and those fish that have their own little light bulbs attached to their heads? They look like aliens. I don't know why anyone would want to go down there on purpose. I won't even go in a swimming pool if I can't see the bottom. 

But um, no, I haven't been feeling restless or having trouble sitting still.
Do you have difficulty concentrating or making decisions?

Yeah, actually, I really do. It's been so frustrating lately. Like, when I try to work on my catering forms or this Chamber of Commerce application I've been meaning to finish, I just... I end up reading the same line over and over again. And then I get completely stuck on these tiny little choices, like what price to put down for a dozen cupcakes or which email I should answer first. 

Speaking of cupcakes, my neighbor just started this cupcake business out of her kitchen, and she brought over a batch of these lavender honey ones to test out. I don't know who told people that flowers belong in baked goods, but it literally tasted like I was eating a bar of fancy soap. I couldn't even finish it, but I had to pretend it was amazing because she was standing right there waiting for my reaction. I ended up wrapping the rest of it in a napkin and throwing it in the trash can at the park down the street so she wouldn't see it in my garbage. That park is getting so overgrown, though. The city hasn't mowed the grass in weeks, and there are these giant dandelions everywhere. When the wind blows, it looks like it's snowing those little white fluffy seeds. My dog loves chasing them, but then he sneezes for like an hour straight afterward. He has terrible allergies. We tried giving him that special allergy kibble, but it smells like old fish and he just pushes it around his bowl with his nose. 

But um, yeah, concentrating and making decisions has been really hard lately. I just get stuck on everything.
Have you had any episodes where you felt slightly better for a few days at a time since this all started?

No, not really. I haven't noticed any days where I felt better, to be honest. It all just kind of blends together. 

Speaking of days blending together, I actually bought this giant wall calendar recently to try and keep track of things. It's one of those glossy ones with a different lighthouse for every month. I don't even like lighthouses, but it was on clearance at the pharmacy. My aunt, though, she is obsessed with them. She has this huge glass curio cabinet in her dining room completely filled with ceramic lighthouse figurines. She dusts them every single Sunday with that lemon furniture spray, and her entire house constantly smells like fake lemons. I can't stand artificial lemon scent. It always reminds me of those hard candies that end up at the bottom of your purse, the ones that get covered in lint. I actually found a butterscotch candy at the bottom of my bag the other day, and it was completely fused to a grocery receipt from like, two years ago. I tried to peel it off, but it was basically cemented on there. I don't even know why I keep receipts anyway, the ink always fades until it's just a blank piece of shiny paper. 

But, um... no. No stretches of feeling better or anything. Just kind of the same.
Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your appetite?

No, I don't think my appetite has changed much. I mean, I'm still eating about the same as I usually do. 

Although, I did try to make this new pasta recipe I saw online the other day. It was supposed to be this creamy garlic parmesan thing, but I think I messed up the sauce because it came out really grainy. I hate when cheese does that, you know? When it doesn't melt right and just turns into these weird little clumps. I ended up having to throw the whole pan out, which made me so mad because cheese is expensive right now. Have you noticed how much groceries have gone up? I went to the store just to get eggs and milk, and I swear it cost me like twenty dollars. And the milk wasn't even the good kind—it was that skim milk that basically just looks like cloudy water. My sister drinks skim milk, and I don't understand how she stands it. She pours it over her cereal and it doesn't even make the cereal soggy, it just kind of washes it. She eats those bran flakes that look like little pieces of cardboard. She claims they're good for digestion, but honestly, I think she just likes punishing herself. I'd rather just eat toast if that's the alternative. I have this toaster that only toasts one side of the bread, though. It's so annoying. I have to stand there and flip the bread halfway through if I want it evenly browned. 

But um, no, my appetite is pretty normal. Nothing really different there.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience any kind of pleasure at all, even briefly?

Yeah, I guess... I mean, I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Like, dance class, hiking, trying new recipes, even game night with my friends... they all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. 

Speaking of game night, my friend Sarah brought over this new board game last time, and it was so complicated. It had like a hundred different tiny wooden pieces, and the instruction manual was practically a novel. We spent an hour just trying to set it up, and by the time we figured out the rules, nobody even wanted to play anymore. Sarah is always buying these intense strategy games that take up the entire dining table. Her dining table is gorgeous, though. It's this solid oak farmhouse table her husband built from scratch. He's really handy like that. He actually built them a chicken coop in their backyard last summer. They got six chickens, and they named them all after old Hollywood actresses. They have a Marilyn, an Audrey, a Katharine... I can't remember the rest. But they lay so many eggs that Sarah is constantly trying to give them away. She brings them over in these recycled cardboard cartons, and the eggs are all different colors—like light blue and speckled brown. I tried boiling some for egg salad, but I always overcook them and the yolks get that weird gray ring around them. It ruins the whole sandwich. 

But um, yeah, I just... I don't really get any joy out of my usual hobbies right now. It all just feels like too much effort.
Have you noticed any changes in how quickly or slowly you're moving or reacting to things compared to how you used to?

No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed moving any slower or faster or anything like that. I feel like I'm moving at my normal speed, I guess. 

Speaking of moving, my neighbor across the hall is moving out this weekend, and she has been making so much noise dragging boxes down the stairs. It's a walk-up, so I get it, but she has this massive collection of vintage encyclopedias that must weigh a ton. I don't even know why people keep physical encyclopedias anymore when everything is on the internet. My dad used to have a set of Encyclopedia Britannica from the 80s, and they took up an entire bookshelf in the living room. The bindings were this dark red leather with gold lettering, and they smelled like old paper and dust. I used to pull them out when I was a kid just to look at the pictures of different dog breeds. I really wanted a Golden Retriever growing up, but my mom was allergic to pet dander. She tried getting me a goldfish instead, but it died after three days. I think I overfed it. The pet store guy said you're only supposed to give them a tiny pinch of flakes, but I felt bad that it was just swimming around in that little bowl with nothing to do, so I kept dropping more food in. The water got all murky and gross. I felt so guilty about it for weeks. 

But um, no, my movements and everything seem pretty normal. I haven't noticed any changes there.
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities is more due to not enjoying them or because you're just not able to motivate yourself to do them?

I think it's... well, it's kind of both, maybe? Like I said before, I just barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Dance class, hiking, trying new recipes... even game night. They all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. I just don't have the motivation, and when I think about doing them, I don't even feel like I'd enjoy them anyway. 

Speaking of chores, my vacuum cleaner broke yesterday, and I'm so annoyed about it. It's one of those expensive cordless ones that you mount on the wall, and the battery just completely died. I only bought it like two years ago. I called customer service, and the guy on the phone—his name was Kevin, I think—was so unhelpful. He just kept telling me to check the filter. Like, obviously I checked the filter, Kevin. It's completely clean. I even washed it out in the sink and let it air dry on the dish rack for 24 hours just like the manual says. The dish rack is getting kind of rusty, actually. I need to buy a new one, maybe one of those bamboo ones. I saw this really cute bamboo dish rack at Target last week when I was looking for a birthday card for my aunt. She just turned 60, and she had this huge party at a country club, but I didn't go. I just sent a card with a gift card inside. I hate country clubs. The grass is always too perfect, and everyone wears those pastel polo shirts. My uncle used to wear those shirts, and he always popped the collar. It looked so ridiculous, especially because he was bald and sunburned all the time. He used to fall asleep in the lawn chair holding a beer, and the dog would come over and lick his toes. We had a basset hound named Buster. He tripped over his own ears once and fell down the porch stairs...

But um, yeah, the lack of interest... it's just really hard to get up the energy to do anything, and I don't think I'd even have fun if I did.
Have you noticed yourself fidgeting, pacing, or feeling an inability to sit still when you're trying to relax?

No, I don't really get like that. I don't have any trouble sitting still or anything. I can just sit on the couch for hours, honestly. 

Speaking of the couch, I really need to get a new slipcover for it. The one I have is this weird beige color, and it shows every single stain. I spilled coffee on it last week—just a little bit, but it left this huge brown ring right in the middle of the middle cushion. I tried scrubbing it out with club soda, but it just made the spot bigger. My sister told me I should just buy a whole new couch, but couches are so expensive right now. I went to a furniture store the other day just to look, and the salesman followed me around the entire time. He was wearing this really cheap cologne that smelled like pine needles and cheap aftershave, and it gave me a headache. I hate strong smells like that. It reminds me of those little tree air fresheners people hang in their cars. My first car was this beat-up Honda Civic, and the previous owner must have smoked in it because it permanently smelled like stale cigarettes and vanilla air fresheners. I tried everything to get the smell out. I even left a bowl of vinegar in the backseat overnight because I read online that it absorbs odors. It didn't work, though. It just made the car smell like a salad dressing factory. I ended up selling it to this kid who was just learning how to drive. He was so excited, he didn't even care about the smell. He had this really cool vintage leather jacket on...

But um, yeah, I don't really fidget or pace or anything. I can sit still just fine.
Do you feel like your current state is severely impacting your daily life and ability to function?

Yeah, I guess it is. I've missed the Chamber application deadlines, and I just keep putting my catering plans on hold because I can't reliably handle the paperwork and the jobs and the people the way I used to. I also see my friends a lot less. I feel like my life has just gotten smaller, kind of shrinking around what feels safe. 

Speaking of catering, I was supposed to make these mini quiches for a friend's baby shower last month, and I completely forgot to buy the Gruyère cheese. You really can't make a good quiche without Gruyère. I tried substituting it with sharp cheddar, but it just wasn't the same. The crust got all soggy on the bottom, too. I think my oven temperature is off. I need to get an oven thermometer, but I always forget when I'm at the store. I went to the grocery store yesterday and walked out with three bags of chips and no milk. I always do that. The cashier was this really young kid, maybe 16, and he had braces with those neon green rubber bands. I had braces when I was in high school, and I hated them. I got the clear ones thinking they'd be less noticeable, but they just stained yellow every time I ate curry or drank tea. My orthodontist was this really old guy who always hummed classical music while he tightened my wires. He had a massive fish tank in his waiting room with these huge angelfish. One time, I saw one of the angelfish eating a smaller fish, and I completely freaked out. I told the receptionist, but she just laughed and said that's nature. Nature is so weird sometimes. Like, did you know that some species of frogs can freeze completely solid in the winter and then just thaw out and hop away in the spring? I saw a documentary about it on PBS. The narrator had this really soothing British accent. I could listen to British people read the phone book, honestly...

But um, yeah, it's definitely impacting my life. The catering, the paperwork, my friends... it's just hard to manage it all right now.
Do you feel like you're unable to find pleasure in anything at all, even small things like taking a warm bath or reading a good book?

Yeah, it's exactly like I was saying earlier. I just... I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. The dance class, the hiking, trying new recipes... even just taking a bath or reading a book. They all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. I tried reading the other day, but it just felt like work. 

Speaking of books, I left a library book on my patio table last week, and it completely warped in the rain. It was a biography about some old Hollywood actress, I can't remember her name. But the pages got all crinkly and stuck together. I had to pay a $25 replacement fee, which is so annoying because the book was probably from the nineties anyway. The librarian who took my payment was giving me such a look, too. She had these really thick, cat-eye glasses that were attached to a pearl chain around her neck. My grandmother used to wear glasses chains like that. She had this huge collection of them—some were beaded, some were gold. She kept them in this old cigar box on her dresser. The box always smelled faintly of tobacco and peppermint, because she kept those little red and white peppermints in her purse. She would always give me one during church so I'd stop fidgeting in the pews. The pews at her church were made of this really hard oak, and they didn't have any cushions. I always got splinters on the back of my legs if I wore a dress. I hated wearing dresses. My mom used to force me into these itchy floral things with the scratchy lace collars for Easter. We always had to take a family photo in front of this big dogwood tree in our front yard, and I was always squinting because the sun was right in my eyes...

But um, yeah, even the small things just feel like chores now. I don't really get any pleasure out of them.
Do you feel like your current state is interfering with your ability to work or take care of daily responsibilities?

Like I was saying a few minutes ago, yeah, it really is. That's why I keep putting my catering plans on hold and why I missed those Chamber of Commerce application deadlines. I just can't reliably handle the paperwork and the jobs and dealing with people the way I used to. I'm seeing my friends a lot less, too. It just feels like my whole life has gotten smaller, shrinking down to just whatever feels safe right now. 

Speaking of paperwork, I actually tried to organize my desk last week to try and get back on track. I bought all these colorful file folders, but I accidentally bought legal size instead of letter size, so they don't even fit in my filing cabinet. My filing cabinet is this heavy, ugly gray metal thing I found at a yard sale a few years ago. The guy running the yard sale had this massive collection of vintage license plates covering his entire garage wall. He told me he collected one from every state, but he was still missing Alaska. I've always wanted to go to Alaska to see the Northern Lights. I had a friend who went on an Alaskan cruise for her honeymoon, and she said the midnight buffet on the ship was incredible. They had this huge chocolate fountain that ran 24/7. I don't know how I feel about chocolate fountains, honestly. People just stick their hands and half-eaten marshmallows in there. It seems really unsanitary. Kind of like those plastic ball pits at fast-food places. When I was little, I lost my favorite mood ring in a ball pit at a birthday party, and I cried for like two hours straight. My mom had to buy me a personal pan pizza just to calm me down. I used to love those little pizzas... 

But um, yeah, like I said before, the daily responsibilities like the catering and the paperwork are just too much for me to handle right now.
Do you feel like you're at a point where you can't even imagine feeling better or enjoying things again?

Yeah, like I keep saying, that's exactly why I came in to begin with. I just... I can't even picture getting back to who I was. I barely care about any of the things that used to make me feel like myself. Like I mentioned, the dance classes, the hiking, trying new recipes, and even game night... they all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. 

Speaking of game night, we used to play Scrabble a lot, and my sister would always try to use fake words. She once tried to play "za," claiming it was short for pizza, and we argued for like twenty minutes. She always had to win. She's a real estate agent now, and her face is on those giant billboards by the highway. I always wonder how they print things that big. Like, is it one giant printer, or do they print it in strips and glue it together? I tried to print out a recipe for lemon bars last week, and my printer just completely jammed. It made this horrible grinding noise, and then all the ink smeared across the page. I got ink all over my fingers, and it took three days to wash off. I tried using dish soap, but it just dried my hands out. My hands get so dry in the winter. I used to buy this really expensive shea butter lotion from a lady at the farmer's market, but she stopped setting up her booth. She told me she was moving to Arizona because the humidity here was bad for her joints. Arizona seems too hot, though. I don't think I could handle the desert. There are scorpions there, and they can hide in your shoes. I always shake my shoes out anyway, just in case a spider got in there. I saw a spider the size of a half-dollar in my bathroom sink once, and I just turned around and used the kitchen sink for two days... 

But um, yeah, like I said, that's why I'm here. I just can't imagine enjoying those things again when they all just feel like chores I have to get through.

My filing cabinet is this heavy, ugly gray metal thing I found at a yard sale a few years ago. The guy running the yard sale had this massive collection of vintage license plates covering his entire garage wall. He told me he collected one from every state, but he was still missing Alaska. I've always wanted to go to Alaska to see the Northern Lights. I had a friend who went on an Alaskan cruise for her honeymoon, and she said the midnight buffet on the ship was incredible. They had this huge chocolate fountain that ran 24/7. I don't know how I feel about chocolate fountains, honestly. People just stick their hands and half-eaten marshmallows in there. It seems really unsanitary. Kind of like those plastic ball pits at fast-food places. When I was little, I lost my favorite mood ring in a ball pit at a birthday party, and I cried for like two hours straight. My mom had to buy me a personal pan pizza just to calm me down. I used to love those little pizzas... 

But um, yeah, like I said before, the daily responsibilities like the catering and the paperwork are just too much for me to handle right now.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive symptoms
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're at a point where you can't even imagine feeling better or enjoying things again?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself—dance class, hiking, trying new recipes, even game night all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the inability to enjoy things again, which directly corresponds to the loss of interest or pleasure in activities.

patient.answer:
Yeah, like I keep saying, that's exactly why I came in to begin with. I just... I can't even picture getting back to who I was. I barely care about any of the things that used to make me feel like myself. Like I mentioned, the dance classes, the hiking, trying new recipes, and even game night... they all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. 

Speaking of game night, we used to play Scrabble a lot, and my sister would always try to use fake words. She once tried to play "za," claiming it was short for pizza, and we argued for like twenty minutes. She always had to win. She's a real estate agent now, and her face is on those giant billboards by the highway. I always wonder how they print things that big. Like, is it one giant printer, or do they print it in strips and glue it together? I tried to print out a recipe for lemon bars last week, and my printer just completely jammed. It made this horrible grinding noise, and then all the ink smeared across the page. I got ink all over my fingers, and it took three days to wash off. I tried using dish soap, but it just dried my hands out. My hands get so dry in the winter. I used to buy this really expensive shea butter lotion from a lady at the farmer's market, but she stopped setting up her booth. She told me she was moving to Arizona because the humidity here was bad for her joints. Arizona seems too hot, though. I don't think I could handle the desert. There are scorpions there, and they can hide in your shoes. I always shake my shoes out anyway, just in case a spider got in there. I saw a spider the size of a half-dollar in my bathroom sink once, and I just turned around and used the kitchen sink for two days... 

But um, yeah, like I said, that's why I'm here. I just can't imagine enjoying those things again when they all just feel like chores I have to get through.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent lack of interest in activities they once enjoyed, a decrease in pleasure, and significant impairment in social and occupational functioning, which have been present for more than two years. These symptoms align with the criteria for Major Depressive Disorder, single episode.
